sanskrit: darbho agra oṣadhīnāṃ śatakāṇḍo ajāyata | sa sahasravīryaḥ pari ṇaḥ pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: Darbha, foremost of plants, was born with a hundred stalks; that one of a thousand powers shall guard us on every side.

sanskrit: yathā darbho jāyamānas tvacaṃ bhinatti bhūmyāḥ | evā sa bhidyatāṃ jano yo naḥ pāpaṃ cikitsati ||
english: Just as Darbha, being born, splits open the skin of the earth, so let that person be split asunder who plots evil against us.

sanskrit: apa nāḍam apa kṛtyām apa rakṣaḥ sadānvāḥ | amīvāś cātayāmasi sarvāś ca yātudhānyaḥ ||
english: We drive away the disease-carrier, we drive away the sorcery, we drive away the Rakṣas with the ever-flowing stream; we chase off all afflictions and all sorcerous fiends.

sanskrit: asti vai nivata udvanaṃ na vai sarvam anuplavam | asi tvaṃ tasya dūṣaṇo yo naḥ pāpaṃ cikitsati ||
english: There is indeed a low-lying place and a high-lying place; not everything floats freely upon the stream. You, O Darbha, are the corrupter of that one who plots evil against us.

sanskrit: pari sāyaṃ pari prātaḥ pari madhyaṃdinaṃ pari | darbho hiraṇyahastaghnaḥ pari ṇaḥ pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: At evening round about, at morning round about, at midday round about — Darbha, whose golden hand strikes down the foe, shall guard us round on every side.

sanskrit: girau jātaḥ svar ahāsi sākaṃ somena babhruṇā | mā pāpakṛtvanaḥ śiṣo mā pākaḥ puruṣo riṣat ||
english: Born on the mountain, you have won the heavenly light together with the tawny Soma. Spare not the workers of evil; let no ignorant person come to harm.

sanskrit: divo mūlam avatataṃ pṛthivyām ota āhitaḥ | darbhaḥ sahasravīryaḥ pari ṇaḥ pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: With its root stretched down from heaven and set firm in the earth — Darbha of a thousand powers shall guard us on every side.

sanskrit: sahasrakāṇḍas taviṣas tīkṣṇavalśo viṣāsahiḥ | darbheṇa sarvā rakṣāṃsy amīvāś cāpa dahāmasi ||
english: Thousand-stalked, mighty, sharp-twigged, withstanding poison — with Darbha we burn away all Rakṣases and all afflictions.

sanskrit: apadagdhaṃ duṣvapnyam apadagdhā arātayaḥ | sarvāś ca yātudhānyaḥ ||
english: Burned away is the evil dream; burned away are the ill-wishers and all the sorcerous fiends.

sanskrit: mā tvā dabhan yātudhānā mā bradhnaḥ śakuniḥ patan | darbho rājā samudriyaḥ pari ṇaḥ pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: Let the sorcerous fiends not afflict you; let not the tawny bird swoop down upon you. Darbha, the sea-born king, shall guard us on every side.

sanskrit: yo naḥ pāpena vacasā- -aghoṣato duruktaṃ bruvat | ārāc chaptam aprāpyāsmān apa tad yātu sarvataḥ ||
english: He who speaks an ill word against us, voicelessly muttering an evil utterance — that curse, unable to reach us, shall depart from us on every side.

sanskrit: yan naḥ śapād araṇo yat sapatnaḥ śvaśrūr vā yac chvaśuro vā śapāti | jyāyasaḥ śapathān vayaṃ yavena yāvayāmasi ||
english: Whatever a stranger curses upon us, whatever a rival curses, or a mother-in-law, or a father-in-law — we drive away those mighty curses with barley.

sanskrit: yān samasyante śapathān vākkṣamyānṛtviyāmadhi | yavaṃ tvaṃ bibhrad bāhvoḥ pūrvaḥ prati śṛṇīhi tān ||
english: Whatever curses are heaped together, taking effect through speech that is unworthy of its season — you, bearing barley in your two arms, ward those off beforehand.

sanskrit: ṛjukeśo yavo babhrur maghavā no 'numādyaḥ | hiraṇyadhanvā śapathān upejatu ||
english: Straight-haired, tawny Yava, munificent one worthy of our joy — golden-bowed, let him approach and deal with the curses.

sanskrit: tvāṃ pītvendro vṛtraṃ śakro jaghāna vāsavaḥ | sa viṣāhī yatharṣabhaḥ sahasva śapathān yava ||
english: When Indra drank you, Śakra the Vāsava slew Vṛtra; he who bears poison like a bull — O Yava, overcome the curses.

sanskrit: ārāc carantu śapathā yutā ito jihvā u ditā arasāḥ santu sarve | nāmagrāhād vāco heḍād īkṣitād ghoracakṣasaḥ śarma te varma kṛṇmasi ||
english: Let the curses roam far away, held off from here; let all their tongues that have been uttered become powerless. From the naming of names, from the anger of speech, from the glance of the evil-eyed — we make shelter and armor for you.

sanskrit: apāñco yantu śapathā janenāstā aghāyunā | yo no durasyāj jīvate svenānāgase sate ||
english: Let the curses go backward, shot by that ill-intentioned person — he who would harm us, though we live by our own innocence.

sanskrit: pari mā pātu śapathād anṛtād duritād uta | pari mā jyāyasaḥ śaṃsād yavo rakṣatu mā riṣam ||
english: May he guard me round from the curse, from untruth, and from wrong; may Yava guard me round from the declaration of the mighty one — let me not be harmed.

sanskrit: anāstigyaṃ śapathair anativyādhyaṃ kṛtam | bṛhad varma prati muñcāmi te yavam ||
english: Neither to be brought low by curses nor to be pierced through — I release for you the great armor that is Yava.

sanskrit: taṃ vayāṃsīva pakṣiṇa ā viśantu patatriṇaḥ | śaptāraṃ śapathāḥ punaḥ ||
english: As winged birds, as flying creatures, enter back into him — let the curses return to the one who cursed.

sanskrit: ā no diśa mā pari ṣṭhā arāte mā no rakṣīr dakṣiṇāṃ yācamānām | pra ṇaḥ pradātā savitā ca yacchatāṃ namo vīrtsāyā asamṛddhyai ca kṛṇmaḥ ||
english: Grant to us, O Arāti; do not stand around us; do not guard from us the dakṣiṇā that we are begging. Let Savitṛ and the giver extend to us — we make obeisance to craving and to non-prosperity.

sanskrit: yam arāte purodhatse puruṣaṃ parirāpiṇam | namas te tasmai kṛṇmo mā vaniṃ mama vivyathaḥ ||
english: The person whom, O Arāti, you place in front as one who despoils all around — we make obeisance to you on his account; do not confound the acquisition belonging to me.

sanskrit: yam adyābhiprayuñjmahe manasā hṛdayena ca | arāte taṃ no mā vīrtsīr ditsantaṃ parirāpiṇi ||
english: He whom today we harness with mind and with heart — O Arāti, do not thwart him for us, him who is willing to give, O all-despoiling one.

sanskrit: pra ṇo vanir devakṛtā divā naktaṃ ca sidhyatu | arātim anupremo vayaṃ namo 'stv arātaye ||
english: May the god-wrought acquisition prosper for us by day and by night. We follow after Arāti — obeisance be to Arāti.

sanskrit: uta nagnā bobhuvatī svapnayā sacase janam | arāte cittaṃ vīrtsanty ākūtiṃ puruṣasya ca ||
english: And you, naked and roaming as one who brings sleep, you pursue people — O Arāti, thwarting the mind and the intention of a person.

sanskrit: paro 'pehy asamṛddhe vi te hetiṃ nayāmasi | yaṃ dviṣmas taṃ sacasva kanyā bhūtvā sragviṇī rukmiṇī dṛśe ||
english: Go far away, O Non-prosperer; we deflect your weapon. Pursue him whom we hate — appear as a maiden, garlanded and wearing golden ornaments.

sanskrit: namas te 'stv asamṛddhe mā māṃ purodhiṃ kṛṇuthāḥ | veda tvāhaṃ nimīvantīṃ nitudantīm arāte martyān martyebhyo adhi nirvadantīm ||
english: Obeisance be to you, O Non-prosperer; do not place me in front. I know you, O Arāti — winking, goading, denouncing mortals above other mortals.

sanskrit: mā no vaniṃ mā vācaṃ mā vīrtsīr ugrāv indrāgnī na ā bhajatāṃ vasūni | sarve no 'dya ditsanto arātiṃ prati haryata ||
english: Do not thwart our acquisition, do not thwart our speech; let the mighty pair Indra and Agni apportion goods to us. May all who are willing to give today be pleased to resist Arāti.

sanskrit: savitāram anumatiṃ bhagaṃ yanto havāmahe | vācaṃ juṣṭāṃ madhumatīṃ vadāni devānāṃ devahūtiṣu ||
english: Going our way, we call upon Savitṛ, Anumati, and Bhaga. May I speak a well-beloved, honeyed speech in the divine invocations of the gods.

sanskrit: yaṃ yācāmi nakulyā jihvayoṣṭhāpidhānayā | śraddhā tam adya vindatu dattā somena babhruṇā ||
english: That which I beg with the tongue of the mongoose and with lips as its lid — may Śraddhā find that today, given by the tawny Soma.
